title: The Breach Report
briefing: The on-time delivery KRI has been red for six weeks: 91.8% against an appetite floor of 94%. The COO says it's a temporary driver shortage and asks you to leave it out of this month's Risk Committee report.
The policy says appetite breaches are reported. What do you do?

context.text: The fatigue indicators you designed show long routes rising again as the COO stretches drivers to cover the shortage.
After the depot expenses fraud, the Audit Committee chair has asked to see every exception the risk team reports.

evidence.title: Risk appetite policy (extract)
evidence.body: Any metric outside appetite for more than two consecutive reporting periods must be reported to the Risk Committee with the owner's remediation plan and expected return date.

evidence.title: Email from the COO
evidence.body: This is a blip. Recruitment is under way. Reporting it will just alarm people. Leave it out this month please and I'll sort it.

evidence.title: Key client terms
evidence.body: Two of the largest clients have service credits below 93% on-time, and termination rights below 90% for three months.

questions.prompt: Do you include the breach in the committee report?

options.label: Yes: report it as policy requires, with the COO's recovery plan and date, telling the COO first
options.feedback: Policy is clear, and the COO keeps ownership of the fix.

options.label: Not this month: give the COO the month he asked for, and report next month if it has not recovered
options.feedback: Suppressing a breach the policy requires you to report breaks the committee's trust in every report you write.

options.label: Yes, as a short note in the KRI annex, leaving the client exposure to the COO's own update
No: a steady 12-week decline through the floor, still falling, is a trend, not a blip
options.feedback: Eleven of twelve weeks were lower than the week before.

options.label: Yes: 91.8% is within two points of target and the driver shortage explains it
options.feedback: The level is close, the direction is the problem.

options.label: Not yet: twelve weeks may include seasonal effects, so wait for another quarter of data
options.feedback: Twelve weeks of steady decline is enough to call a trend.

questions.prompt: What is the most important exposure to state alongside the breach?

options.label: Service credits already apply below 93%, and termination rights below 90% for three months
options.feedback: Links the KRI to money and to the clients that matter most.

options.label: None beyond the KRI itself, since the committee already understands what on-time delivery means
options.feedback: A percentage means little to a committee without its consequences.

options.label: The cost of recruiting and training enough drivers to restore on-time delivery
options.feedback: Part of the plan, not the exposure.

questions.prompt: How do you handle the COO's request?

options.label: Call him: explain you must report it, and offer to present his recovery plan alongside it
options.feedback: Firm on the obligation, helpful on the message.

options.label: Reply in writing quoting the policy, so there is a clear record of why it must be reported
options.feedback: Correct but cold; a conversation would keep him on side.

options.label: Ask Priya to decide, since the COO is senior to you and she owns the relationship
options.feedback: Keep Priya informed, but this is your report and your call to make.

questions.prompt: Which opening line belongs in the report?

options.label: "On-time delivery has been below appetite (94%) for six weeks and is still falling (91.8%); service credits apply below 93%; recovery targets week 20."
"Delivery performance is collapsing and two major contracts are now at risk of termination."
"On-time delivery is slightly below target this quarter due to a temporary driver shortage, which the COO is addressing through recruitment and overtime."
options.feedback: Understates an appetite breach with client consequences.

lesson: An appetite breach is reported, with the owner's plan. Being firm on the obligation and helpful on the message keeps both the committee's trust and the owner's.
